clue.text: Subtlety about beautiful chess pieces brought by tournament's leader

parts.note: re is a short Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning
fine can mean beautiful or handsome
men is a standard word for the pieces in chess or draughts

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter, so only the start of tournament's is used

explanation.surface: A connoisseur admires an elegant chess set presented by the head of a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: Refinement is fineness of distinction or delicacy, the same quality as subtlety.

clue.text: Enthusiastically praise party

definitions.meaning: to ... about something is to praise it with great enthusiasm
a large lively party, especially with dance music

explanation.definitionFit: Rave is both a verb for gushing praise and a noun for a wild dance party.

clue.text: More of us playing, around South, this form of golf

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the South letter
playing suggests moving about, so the letters of more of us are rearranged

explanation.surface: More of us want to play round the southern course in this format of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' makes FOURSOME from MORE OF US, and 'around' puts S inside before the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Foursomes is a golf format in which two pairs play, partners hitting alternate shots with one ball.

clue.text: Native from Botswana talking

indicators.note: from signals that the letters are taken out of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: Someone born in Botswana is speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal relates to birth, so it means native in the sense of one's birthplace.

clue.text: Climbed hill around outskirts of Trowbridge

indicators.note: around means enclosing, so the hill word surrounds the town's edges

parts.note: a mound is a small hill

indicators.note: outskirts are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of the town are used

explanation.surface: Someone scaled a hill on the edge of a Wiltshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' gives TE from Trowbridge, a town in Wiltshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount a slope or a horse is to climb onto or up it, so mounted means climbed.

clue.text: Monica worried about daughter travelling

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled name goes around the daughter letter
worried suggests being agitated or shaken, so the letters of Monica are rearranged

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Monica frets about her daughter, who is always on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' turns MONICA into NOMAIC, and 'about' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic means wandering from place to place, living a travelling life.

clue.text: Fancy wife going with that man

parts.note: him refers to a male person, that man

explanation.surface: A married man suspects his wife has taken a fancy to another fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A whim is a sudden fancy or passing desire, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Excited, male sheep used for breeding

parts.note: he refers to a male
a tup is a ram, a male sheep kept for breeding

explanation.surface: A ram kept for breeding is in a lively state.
explanation.definitionFit: Het up is an informal phrase meaning agitated or worked up, i.e. excited.

clue.text: London landmark, indistinct during parade

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the indistinct word goes inside the parade word

parts.note: a march is a parade or procession
blear means dim or blurred, indistinct

explanation.surface: A London monument appears hazy in the middle of a procession.
explanation.walkthrough: MARBLE ARCH is a triumphal arch near the north-east corner of Hyde Park in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Marble Arch is a famous monument in central London, an example of a landmark.

clue.text: Participating, and winning

definitions.meaning: ... in something means taking part in it
winning in the sense of charming or attractive, as in a winning smile

explanation.definitionFit: Engaging means both taking part and charming or appealing.

clue.text: Clear chamber

definitions.meaning: to clear an obstacle is to leap over it
an underground chamber or strongroom, as in a bank

explanation.definitionFit: Vault means both to jump over something and an arched or secure storage room.

clue.text: On high church in a London suburb

parts.note: up means on high, aloft
a minster is a large or important church, such as York Minster

explanation.surface: A lofty church stands somewhere in the outskirts of London.
explanation.walkthrough: UPMINSTER is a district at the eastern end of London's Underground District line.
explanation.definitionFit: Upminster is a named suburban district in east London, an example of a London suburb.

clue.text: Vague details about duck put in quarantine

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the duck
vague suggests imprecise or muddled, so the letters of details are jumbled

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nothing, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Sketchy information emerges about a duck being kept in quarantine, perhaps for bird flu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O inside ISLATED, the anagram of DETAILS made by 'Vague'.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate someone is to keep them apart, so isolated is a past-participle synonym of quarantined.

clue.text: Horrify a friend parking in the centre

indicators.note: the parking letter is placed in the middle of the word for friend

parts.note: a pal is a friend
P is the standard abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A friend is horrified at someone parking right in the middle of town.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to fill with horror or dismay, a verb synonym of horrify.

clue.text: Artist in Baltic country volunteers for operatic work

indicators.note: in places the artist inside the name of the Baltic country

parts.note: Latvia is a country on the Baltic Sea
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A painter in Latvia takes on volunteers to help stage an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: La Traviata is an opera by Verdi, so it is an operatic work.

clue.text: Member leading group of players? This may confirm it

definitions.text: Member leading group of players? This may confirm it

indicators.note: leading means coming first, so the limb word goes before the band word

parts.note: an arm is a member, meaning a limb of the body
a band is a group of musicians, players of instruments

explanation.surface: Is this player the team's leader? The badge on the sleeve will tell you.
explanation.walkthrough: A football or cricket captain wears an armband to show they lead the team, so the whole clue defines the answer as well as building it.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain's armband is worn to show which member of a team is its leader.

clue.text: Tune for church service

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody
taken as written
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A hymn tune is chosen for a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like a church service, but it means one of the armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: The air force is one of the armed services, alongside the army and navy.

clue.text: Monster — little child, Marie, being naughty

parts.note: ch is the short form of child, so a little child is the abbreviation

indicators.note: naughty suggests misbehaving, so the letters of Marie are jumbled

explanation.surface: A small girl called Marie is being a little monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' signals shortening child to its abbreviation CH; 'being naughty' turns MARIE into IMERA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chimera is a fire-breathing beast of Greek myth, a classic monster.

clue.text: A rose, say, worker planted in row

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg

indicators.note: planted in means set inside, so the worker goes into the row word

parts.note: a line is a row
an ant is a worker, from the worker caste of the ant colony

explanation.surface: A gardener sets a rose, for instance, in a neat row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A rose' is the definition on its own; 'say' is the usual crossword signal for 'for example', abbreviated EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a species of wild rose.

clue.text: Dubious sort with alcoholic drink on platform

indicators.note: dubious suggests something not straight, so the letters of sort are rearranged

parts.note: rum is a spirit, an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A shady character holding a glass of spirits stands on the platform.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform for a speaker or conductor.

clue.text: As if I'm bothered about old criminals

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the old letter
bothered means flustered, so the letters of as if I'm are mixed up

explanation.surface: A careless remark: as if I'm worried about old crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bothered' gives MAFISI from AS IF I'M, and 'about' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mafiosi are members of the Mafia, an organised crime network, so they are criminals.

clue.text: Divine decoration for cakes, trimmed

indicators.note: trimmed means cut back, so the final letter of the cake decoration is dropped

parts.note: angelica is a plant whose candied green stems are used to decorate cakes

explanation.surface: A heavenly cake gets its decoration pared down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimmed' removes the last A from ANGELICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelic means like an angel, heavenly, so it is an adjective synonym of divine.

clue.text: Simple-minded person needing help to catch flightless bird

indicators.note: catching means enclosing, so the help word goes around the bird

parts.note: aid means help
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: A dimwit needs assistance to catch a bird that cannot fly.
explanation.definitionFit: An airhead is an informal term for a foolish, empty-headed person.

clue.text: Sign right in the middle of Galician port

indicators.note: the letter for right is placed inside the name of the Spanish port

parts.note: Vigo is a port city in Galicia, north-west Spain

explanation.surface: A signpost points right, straight through the middle of a Spanish harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgo is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Old-style resort, resort without sun

indicators.note: the second resort is a verb, to sort again, so the letters are rearranged
without means lacking, so the sun letter is removed

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for sun or Sunday

explanation.surface: A retro holiday resort is remodelled without its sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes S from RESORT to give RESORT minus S, RETOR; the second 'resort' then rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro describes styles imitating the fashions of the past, i.e. old-style.

clue.text: Old coin, out-of-the-way object

parts.note: a far place is remote, out of the way
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: An antique coin turns up as a curious object in some remote spot.
explanation.walkthrough: A FARTHING was a British coin worth a quarter of an old penny, withdrawn in 1960.
explanation.definitionFit: The farthing was a pre-decimal British coin, so it is an example of an old coin.

clue.text: Pigeon in front of railing

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pigeon perches in front of the railings.
explanation.definitionFit: A homer is a homing pigeon, trained to fly back to its loft.

clue.text: Inferior, the French steamship

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A French steamship is judged second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Less can mean lower in rank or importance, as in no less a person, so it means inferior.

clue.text: On back of lorry, the man's holding fine vegetable

indicators.note: the second part is placed after, on the back of, the lorry word

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a big truck in British usage

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the word for fine sits inside

parts.note: the man's is read as the man is, which is he
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A driver on the back of a truck clutches a choice vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: An artic is the British name for an articulated lorry; 'the man's' is read as 'the man is', so it gives a pronoun rather than a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is a thistle-like plant eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Leading European state

parts.note: main means chief or leading

explanation.surface: A prominent European statesman is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is a US state in New England, an example of a state.

clue.text: Clergyman must get rid of cold soon

indicators.note: getting rid of something means removing it, so the cold letter is taken out

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A vicar with a chill is told to shake it off quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old-fashioned word for shortly or in a little while, meaning soon.

clue.text: Fierce eagles crossing small desert

parts.note: wild means untamed or fierce

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so the eagles word spans the small letter

parts.note: ernes are sea eagles, a crossword favourite
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Savage birds of prey fly over a small stretch of desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A wilderness is an uninhabited waste land, the same as a desert.
